chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Sayābah, from al-Ḥasan ibn Abī Sārah, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام:
We mix with the Jews, the Christians, and the Magians, and we enter upon them while they are eating and drinking; then their cupbearer passes by and pours wine onto my clothes.
So he said: “There is no harm in it, unless you would like to wash it because of its trace.”

key_terms.النَّصَارَى: the Christians mentioned as a community with whom Muslims interact
key_terms.الْخَمْرَ: wine, the substance spilled onto the clothing
key_terms.الْمَجُوسَ: the Magians or Zoroastrians mentioned in the social context of the report
key_terms.الْيَهُودَ: the Jews mentioned as a community with whom Muslims interact
key_terms.ثِيَابِيَ: my clothes, referring to the garment affected by the spill
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or problem in the situation described
key_terms.لِأَثَرِهِ: because of its trace, meaning the remaining mark or effect

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if wine is spilled on one’s clothes in a social setting?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a practical ruling about wine falling onto one’s clothing while visiting non-Muslims. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that there is no problem with it, though washing it due to its visible trace is permissible if one wishes.
